notes: Twelve upper-division courses total, taught in Spanish. Catalog frames requirements at the upper-division level; lower-division language preparation (advanced Spanish proficiency) is assumed but not itemized as major courses on the page. Secondary-language requirement must be in a language other than Spanish. Structure corroborated by catalog; exact lower-division prerequisites not itemized verbatim.

buckets.label: Upper-division advanced Spanish
buckets.note: One course in advanced Spanish reading/writing: LTSP 100A, 100B, or 100F.

buckets.label: Upper-division pre-1900 requirement
buckets.note: One course in Spanish Peninsular or Latin American literature before 1900, from department-specified lists.

buckets.label: Upper-division Spanish/Latin American/Chicano literature
buckets.note: Seven additional upper-division courses in Spanish, Latin American, and/or Chicano literature (taught in Spanish).

buckets.label: Upper-division electives
buckets.note: Additional upper-division electives from the Department of Literature to reach twelve upper-division courses total.

buckets.label: Secondary-language requirement
buckets.note: At least one course in a secondary language or literature (taught in a language other than Spanish). UCSD LIT-ug: 'At least one course in a secondary language or literature; that is, a course taught in a language other than Spanish.' Satisfied by completing a course (not by proficiency/exam). Any Literature-department language/literature course outside Spanish (LTSP) qualifies; the catalog notes English is an acceptable secondary language for Spanish majors, so English-language literature courses (LTEN/LTWL) count as well. Ranges cover both lower- and upper-division since the requirement does not specify division. LTSP is excluded (it is taught in Spanish).
